assessments.rationale: Analogy A directly mirrors the cache‑coherence idea of multiple copies and instant propagation, covering the key description elements, while B describes a lack of propagation. Both use the same library domain, so conceptual distance is equal, but A’s mapping is clearer and more consistent.

Analogy A captures writes triggering invalidations and maintaining consistency, matching the description. Analogy B flips the mechanism, reducing coverage and internal consistency. Both remain in the distributed‑database domain, so M is unchanged.

Analogy A stays close to the library‑catalog metaphor and covers the essential coherence steps. Analogy B stretches the mapping to social‑media likes, increasing conceptual distance (higher M) but losing some description coverage and structural tightness.

Both analogies describe autonomous drones sharing an obstacle map and instantly broadcasting updates. They are virtually identical in content, structure, and domain, yielding equal scores across all metrics.

Analogy A is a literal description of cache coherence with cores, reads, writes and propagation, covering the description fully. Analogy B uses traffic‑light metaphor, which is farther from the original domain, raising M, while providing less direct coverage and a looser structural mapping.

The two chef analogies are rephrasings of the same idea: shared recipe copies and instant distribution of changes. They equally cover the description, have identical internal mappings, and remain in the same culinary domain.
